sn47.11:1.2: Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn47.11:1.3: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘a great man, a great man.’
sn47.11:1.4: In what way, venerable sir, is one a great man?”
sn47.11:1.5: “With a liberated mind, I say, Sāriputta, one is a great man.
sn47.11:1.6: Without a liberated mind, I say, one is not a great man.
sn47.11:2.1: “And how, Sāriputta, does one have a liberated mind?
sn47.11:2.2: Here, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.11:2.3: As he dwells contemplating the body in the body, the mind becomes dispassionate, and by nonclinging it is liberated from the taints.
sn47.11:2.6: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.11:2.7: As he dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, the mind becomes dispassionate, and by nonclinging it is liberated from the taints.
sn47.11:2.8: “It is in such a way, Sāriputta, that one has a liberated mind.
sn47.11:2.9: With a liberated mind, I say, Sāriputta, one is a great man.
sn47.11:2.10: Without a liberated mind, I say, one is not a great man.”
